They've batted two full sessions, adding 205 runs in 54 overs, and are still unscathed. Starting the day at 291/7, India A added 55 runs to their overnight total, with Jurel bringing up his century and Akash Deep notching up a fifty by playing his shots. Siraj and Mukesh Kumar were relentless in the 8-over phase with the new ball, reducing the home team to 13/3 at lunch. That's when Boyle and Foxcroft joined forces. Not only did they keep the bowlers at bay but also scored at a brisk rate, mixing caution with aggression. Washington Sundar created a chance when Foxcroft was on 20 but Jurel couldn't effect a tough stumping chance. The right-hander also survived a few close lbw appeals. Boyle, on the other hand, batted more fluently and was the aggressor after the tea break. The 23-year-old left-hander got to his century off 141 balls with a well-timed pull shot. New Zealand A will be the happier side at the end of the second day's play. Will they consolidate their position? Or will the visitors stage a comeback? Tune in tomorrow to find out.. 18:24 Local Time, 05:24 GMT, 10:54 IST: The umpires have taken the players off the field as the light has deteriorated and it's not good enough to continue play. Bad light is the reason they went off but it will be Stumps as well.
